title: The Earliest Moment When Everyone Become Friends
summary: Given n people labeled from 0 to n-1, and a series of friendship logs where each log indicates two people becoming friends at a specific timestamp, determine the earliest time when everyone is acquainted with everyone else.
statement: Given n people labeled from 0 to n-1, and a series of friendship logs where each log indicates two people becoming friends at a specific timestamp, determine the earliest time when everyone is acquainted with everyone else. If no such time exists, return -1. Friendship is mutual, and acquaintance is defined by direct or indirect friendships.
constraints: Return the earliest timestamp when all n people are connected, or -1.
hints: Sort events because connectivity only grows over time.
Union the endpoints and track the number of components.
Return the timestamp when a successful union reduces components to one.
That first chronological moment is exactly when everyone shares one connected component.
editorial: That first chronological moment is exactly when everyone shares one connected component.
